predictions: No reproducible allele-specific TF binding at this base.
No allele-specific regulatory activity attributable to rs13078086 in HCT116.
Any disease signal is explained by a linked causal variant, a passenger event, or no allelic regulatory effect.

chains.title: TFAP2E binds the ref allele more strongly through an AP-2 motif near a dELS
chains.element: The variant is 42 bp from dELS EH38E2269392 and does not overlap a cCRE; it may alter an AP-2 site within or next to that element, but this is not established.

links.claim: TFAP2E is nominated because its own QBiC-SELEX model shows the ref T allele binds more strongly than the alt G allele (z -18.37, effect -0.765), and TFAP2E is the highest-expressed AP-2 candidate in HCT116 at 8.5 TPM. The AP-2 family shares binding specificity, and mapped AP-2 models also detect the same ref-more effect for TFAP2A and TFAP2C, so TFAP2E-specific attribution is not established. No ENCODE TFAP2E ChIP data exist and no ChIP peak contains this site, so occupancy is unknown.

The variant is 42 bp from dELS EH38E2269392 and may modify an AP-2 site in or adjacent to that element; because the variant does not overlap a cCRE, direct regulatory-element perturbation is not shown.

PYDC2 is the nearest protein-coding gene at 19.5 kb and the variant is intronic in PYDC2-AS1; no significant GTEx v8 single-tissue eQTL for this variant is reported, so target-gene linkage is not demonstrated.
The mechanism would require TFAP2E occupancy in HCT116; TFAP2E is expressed there, but ENCODE has no TFAP2E ChIP data in HCT116 and no occupancy is shown at the variant.
Colorectal cancer relevance is speculative: rs13078086 has no GWAS Catalog association and no Open Targets record.

predictions: The ref T allele shows stronger TFAP2E binding than the alt G allele.
TFAP2E occupancy at or near rs13078086 would be detectable if assayed in HCT116.
The alt G allele would reduce TFAP2E occupancy and may change PYDC2 expression.
falsified_if: TFAP2E ChIP/CUT&RUN in HCT116 shows no occupancy at rs13078086.
Allele-specific assays show equal TFAP2E binding for T and G.
The AP-2 motif effect is shown to be driven by TFAP2A or TFAP2C rather than TFAP2E.

chains.title: EBF4 binds the ref allele more strongly at a nearby dELS and may regulate PYDC2
chains.element: The variant is 42 bp from dELS EH38E2269392 and does not overlap a cCRE; it may perturb an adjacent element, but direct element overlap is not demonstrated.

links.claim: EBF4 is nominated because its own QBiC-SELEX model gives the largest allelic effect and shows the ref T allele binds more strongly than the alt G allele (z -60.28, effect -1.954). This is weak without occupancy: no ENCODE TF ChIP-seq peak contains the site in any biosample, EBF4 has no ENCODE HCT116 ChIP data, and EBF4 is expressed at only 1.22 TPM in HCT116.
The variant is 42 bp from the dELS EH38E2269392 and may modify an EBF4 site within or adjacent to that element; because no cCRE overlaps the variant, this is proximity evidence only.

PYDC2 is the nearest protein-coding gene, 19.5 kb upstream, and the variant lies in a PYDC2-AS1 intron; however, there are no significant GTEx v8 single-tissue eQTLs for this variant, so the variant-to-PYDC2 link is proximity-based only.
The proposed mechanism would require EBF4 occupancy in HCT116; EBF4 is expressed there at low level, but there is no EBF4 ChIP data in HCT116 and no ENCODE peak at the variant.
Colorectal cancer relevance is unproven: rs13078086 has no GWAS Catalog association and no Open Targets record.

predictions: The ref T allele shows stronger EBF4 binding than the alt G allele.
EBF4 occupancy, if assayed in HCT116, would be detectable at or very near rs13078086.
The alt G allele would reduce EBF4 occupancy and may alter PYDC2 or nearby target expression.

Colorectal cancer relevance is unproven: rs13078086 has no GWAS Catalog association and no Open Targets record.

grades_v0.reason: QBiC-SELEX shows ref allele binds more (z -60.28, effect -1.954), direction consistent. But there is no occupancy evidence: E04 reports no ENCODE TF ChIP-seq peak at this base in any biosample and EBF4 was never assayed. Under the binding rule, QBiC-SELEX alone is weak. EBF4 is also lowly expressed in HCT116 (1.22 TPM), weakening the cell-type rationale.

E03 shows the variant does not overlap any cCRE and the nearest dELS is 42 bp away. Proximity is consistent with a nearby regulatory element, but it does not establish that rs13078086 lies in or perturbs EH38E2269392.

E01/E02 support that PYDC2 is the nearest protein-coding gene (19.5 kb upstream) and that the variant is intronic in PYDC2-AS1. E07 shows no significant GTEx eQTL. This is proximity-based target inference only, not a demonstrated variant-to-PYDC2 expression link.
E10 shows EBF4 is expressed in DepMap ACH-000971/HCT116, but only at 1.22 TPM, and E04 shows no ENCODE EBF4 ChIP data in HCT116. The cell-type claim is conditional on an unmeasured occupancy event.

E05 and E06 directly support the negative statement that there is no GWAS Catalog association and no Open Targets record for rs13078086. This supports only absence of positive disease evidence, not a colorectal cancer phenotype link.

QBiC-SELEX for the TFAP2E record shows ref allele binds more (z -18.37, effect -0.765), direction consistent. No occupancy evidence exists; TFAP2E was never assayed by ENCODE, and E04 reports no peak at this base. E11/E12 also use a TFAP2E-mapped model for TFAP2A/TFAP2C, so the AP-2 signal cannot be cleanly assigned to TFAP2E without additional evidence.
E03 shows no cCRE overlap and a nearest dELS 42 bp away. This supports only adjacency, not that the variant modifies an AP-2 site within EH38E2269392.

PYDC2 is nearest and the variant is in PYDC2-AS1, but there is no eQTL or perturbation evidence linking the base to PYDC2 expression. The claim is proximity-based and explicitly notes no GTEx support.
TFAP2E is expressed in HCT116 at 8.5 TPM, but ENCODE has no TFAP2E ChIP data in HCT116 and no occupancy is shown. Expression alone does not establish the proposed cell-type mechanism.
E05/E06 support only the absence of GWAS/Open Targets evidence for this variant; they do not establish a colorectal cancer phenotype link.

QBiC-SELEX shows alt allele binds more (z 13.11, effect 0.251), direction consistent, and ETV3 is expressed in HCT116 (16.34 TPM). However, there is no occupancy evidence; ETV3 was never assayed by ENCODE and no peak contains the variant. The best model is annotated as a CIS-BP-mapped ETV5 model, so the TF attribution is also weaker than the chain implies.

E05/E06 support only that no GWAS/Open Targets disease association is recorded; this is absence of positive phenotype evidence, not support for a colorectal cancer effect.

checks.why: Direct occupancy is the largest missing piece for the strongest QBiC-SELEX effect; a peak would upgrade H1.binding, while no peak in HCT116 would further weaken it.

next_experiment: The cheapest single experiment separating the top two chains, H0_null and H2_TFAP2E_ref, is an allele-specific TFAP2E EMSA or competitive binding assay with T and G oligos in HCT116 nuclear extract, ideally with TFAP2E antibody supershift. It is binding-only: a positive result supports H2_TFAP2E_ref at the binding link but does not prove occupancy; a negative result falsifies H2_TFAP2E_ref's central TFAP2E-binding claim.

QBiC-SELEX screen of chr3:191441666:T>G, one line per TF, each with the TF's own or CIS-BP-mapped model of largest |z|. Candidates are TFs whose ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant and that are expressed (DepMap line ACH-000971), bound here before bound elsewhere, then a strong site before a weak one, then by |z|; then expressed TFs ENCODE never assayed whose best model passes the gate (occupancy unknown). Shown: 0 of 0 occupied (0 with a strong site), 5 of 85 with unknown occupancy. Left out: 16 TFs assayed in the matching biosample and 557 assayed only elsewhere, none with a peak here. The gate (|z| > 4.05, Bonferroni over 997 models) marks a change QBiC-SELEX detects; it says nothing about occupancy. Effect > 0 means the alternate allele binds more strongly. In vitro binding only. Site strength is the better allele's best k-mer over the variant, as a percentile of the best model's k-mers; a strong site reaches the 97.5th.
